To report a rare case of Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) presenting with early-onset eyelid sebaceous carcinoma in an Asian patient.

A 36-year-old Korean woman presented with a gradually enlarging left lower eyelid mass. Biopsy confirmed sebaceous carcinoma. Her medical history included acute promyelocytic leukemia at age 29, glioblastoma at age 33, and parotid gland cancer at age 34. Li-Fraumeni Syndrome (LFS) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene, conferring a markedly increased lifetime risk of multiple early-onset malignancies. Pediatric patients are particularly susceptible to developing soft tissue sarcomas, osteosarcomas, adrenocortical carcinomas, central nervous system tumors, and hematologic malignancies, necessitating early recognition and lifelong surveillance.
